title: Seascape Photoshop workflow: sky blend, beams, and depth

date.basis: Embedded file creation time indicates 2025-07-06; transcript contains no date; no explicit shooting date inferred from dialogue

summary: This video demonstrates a Photoshop-based post-processing workflow applied to a seascape composite featuring an island and a moving boat. The presenter begins by testing dynamic range and exposure, then crops and adjusts foreground/background elements. A sky layer is introduced and blended with targeted whites and color adjustments, followed by selective layer separation and masking to manage multi-element edits. Beams of light are painted into the scene with a hard brush and then refined by erasing with a soft brush, and additional elements such as birds are added. Shading and warmth are used to impart three-dimensionality to the island and water, aided by clarity and dehaze to create glow. The workflow culminates in sky-focused color grading, a subtle gradient to smooth the transition, and cleanup of dust spots visible at high f-stops. Overall, the video showcases a compact, multi-layer compositing approach to achieve a sunrise-toned, high-contrast seascape in roughly five minutes of editing time.
topics: White and color adjustments for sky
Edge handling during selection and editing
Beams (light rays) creation with 60% hard brush at 1000 px radius
Beams erasing with soft brush for natural look
Clarity and dehaze to create midground glow
Dust spot management at high f-stops

sections.description: This section traces a condensed post-production sequence on a seascape image, starting with dynamic range and exposure exploration, followed by cropping and foreground/background balancing. The workflow then introduces a sky layer for selective color/white adjustments, applies layer separation to manage different elements, and experiments with beam-like light rays and limited-opacity sky blends to integrate the sky. Further steps add depth through warmth and dehaze, reinforce directional lighting on the island, insert decorative birds, and finish with targeted color grading, gradient work, and dust spot cleanup to produce the final composite.
